newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-UEFA ASKS PORTUGAL TO INVESTIGATE BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA ASKS PORTUGAL TO INVESTIGATE BRIBERY ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: UEFA, European soccer's governing body, confirmed on Wednesday that it had asked the Portuguese Football Association to investigate allegations of match fixing.

UEFA made the request after Fernando Barata, the former director of a Portuguese soccer club, said on Monday that he acted as go-between for Porto in a bribery attempt before a match 12 years ago with Scotland's Aberdeen.
"We have asked the Portuguese Football Association to explain what has happend -- that's all," said UEFA spokesman Massimo Gonnella. "Right now we cannot do anything.
"We cannot base a decision to conduct our own investigation from press reports.
"If there is a reason for UEFA to start its own inquiry, it will."

Barata, who has hotel interests in Portugal's southern Algarve region, told TSF radio that he had approached a Romanian referee who had charge of the 1984 European Cup Winners' Cup semifinal between the two clubs.
